entitySuffixRule: Must contain the words "limited liability company" or the abbreviation "L.L.C." or "LLC" or any other similar abbreviation. The name may contain the name of a member or manager, and it may not state or imply that the company is organized for a purpose other than one permitted by RSA 304-C:21 and by its certificate of formation.
distinguishabilityNote: The name must be distinguishable from, and not the same as, six categories on the Secretary of State's records: the name of an entity incorporated, authorized, formed or registered in New Hampshire under RSA 292, 293-A, 293-B, 294-A, 301, 301-A, 304-A, 304-B, 304-C, 305-A or the trade name chapter RSA 349; a name reserved under RSA 293-A, 293-B, 304-A, 304-B or 304-C; the fictitious name of another foreign entity authorized here; the name of a United States, state or subdivision agency or instrumentality, including names reserved under RSA 53-E; the name of a political party recognized under RSA 652:11, absent written consent from its authorized representative; and "farmers' market" unless the entity meets the RSA 21:34-a, V definition. Ten differences do not distinguish: an article, a plural form, phonetic spelling, an abbreviation in place of the full spelling, a prefix or suffix or other derivative of the same word (antonyms and opposites excepted), a change in an entity-status word, an added numeric designation absent the current holder's consent, punctuation or special characters unless they change the clear meaning, whether letters or numbers are separated by spaces, and an Arabic numeral against the Roman numeral or the written word for the same number in the same position. There are four ways through: written consent of the holder, or added words where the name is identical; consent plus an undertaking satisfactory to the Secretary of State to change the other name; a certified copy of a final court judgment establishing the applicant's right to the name; and, without any application, use of another entity's name where the LLC has merged with it, was formed by its reorganization, or has acquired all or substantially all of its assets including the name.
distinguishabilityCitation: RSA 304-C:32, III, III-a, IV, V and VI
nameReservationCostBasis: The Secretary of State fee for an Application for Reservation of Name is $15.
notes: New Hampshire's LLC Act (RSA 304-C) sets a strict two-pronged screen: a name must be both distinguishable from and not the same as the listed names, and RSA 304-C:32, III(a) folds registered trade names (RSA 349) into it, so an active trade name blocks a later LLC name. The ten factors in paragraph III-a mean a prefix, a plural, a phonetic spelling, an abbreviation, an added number, a spacing change or a punctuation change will not clear a conflict. There is no banned-word list in the section; the only word-level bars are "farmers' market" and the name of a recognized political party, both in paragraph III. Two carve-outs run the other way: paragraph VII says the act does not control the use of fictitious names, and paragraph VIII lets the owner of a trade name registered under RSA 349 form an LLC under that same name. The reservation is RSA 304-C:27, not RSA 304-C:32: it runs 120 days, may be renewed for successive 120-day periods, and may be transferred or cancelled by a signed filing. New Hampshire's LLC formation fee and annual report are each $102 (a $100 fee plus a $2 online surcharge), and the annual report is due April 1.
